messages.content: When will be sunset in Beijing today?

function.name: calculate_sunrise
function.description: Calculate the time of sunrise for a specific date and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which sunrise time needs to be calculated.

date.description: The date for which sunrise time needs to be calculated in YYYY-MM-DD format. If not provided, current date is considered. Default: 1998-12-03

format.description: Format in which the time should be returned. If not provided, default format 'HH:MM' is considered.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have a built‑in function to calculate sunset times. I can help you find an online resource or guide you on how to estimate it manually if that would be useful.
message.reasoning: The user asks "When will be sunset in Beijing today?" They want the sunset time. We have a tool to calculate sunrise but not sunset. There's no direct function for sunset. We can approximate or we can say we don't have a function. But maybe we can use the sunrise function with a different parameter? No, it's only sunrise. So we cannot compute sunset directly. We could respond that we can't compute sunset because there's no function. Or we could approximate using sunrise plus day length? But that's too complex. Better to say we don't have a function.
